17	# LaTeX 论文写作全流程
18	
19	ML/AI 顶会论文从草稿到投稿的完整指南。整合 Orchestra Research、VibeSkills、claim2evidence 三方最佳实践。
20	
21	---
22	
23	## 1. 工作模式
24	
25	开始前选择模式：
26	
27	| 模式 | 说明 | 适用 |
28	|------|------|------|
29	| **Build** | 从实验笔记/结果/代码生成论文 | 新稿 |
30	| **Improve** | 改写已有章节，强化论证 | 修改稿 |
31	| **Audit** | 输出风险列表 + 缺失证据 + 修复建议 | 投前检查 |
32	
33	---
34	
35	## 2. Claim-Evidence 方法论
36	
37	**核心原则：论文是一个有中心贡献的故事，不是实验的堆砌。**
38	
39	### 2.1 一句话贡献
40	
41	在写任何内容之前，必须能用一句话说清贡献。如果不能，说明还没准备好写论文。
42	
43	### 2.2 Claim-Evidence Map
44	
45	为每个 contribution 建立 claim→evidence 映射表：
46	
47	| Contribution | Claim | Evidence | Table/Figure |
48	|-------------|-------|----------|-------------|
49	| C1: 方法 X 在 Y 上 SOTA | 比所有 baseline 高 ≥2% | 5-seed 平均，p<0.05 | Table 1 |
50	| C2: 消融证明 Z 是关键 | 去掉 Z 后掉 >5% | 消融实验 | Table 2 |
51	| C3: 计算效率 | 比 baseline 快 3× | FLOPs + wall-clock | Figure 3 |
52	
53	**没有直接证据支撑的 claim 必须删除或降级为 discussion。**
54	
55	### 2.3 章节起草顺序
56	
57	```
58	1. Introduction + Experiments（先确定 claim 和 evidence）
59	2. Method（评估问题稳定后再写细节）
60	3. Related Work
61	4. Abstract + Title（核心 claim 定型后最后写）
62	```
63	
64	### 2.4 Quality Gates
65	
66	投稿前必须通过：
67	- [ ] 前两段出现显式 novelty 声明
68	- [ ] 每个 contribution 有可验证的 evidence
69	- [ ] Abstract / Intro / Conclusion 的 claim 一致
70	- [ ] Limitations 真实且技术性诚实
71	- [ ] 审稿人两分钟内能识别 delta
72	
73	---
74	
75	## 3. 引用防幻觉（CRITICAL）
76	
77	**AI 生成引用有 ~40% 错误率。绝对禁止凭记忆写 BibTeX。**
78	
79	### 3.1 黄金法则
80	
81	```
82	IF 无法程序化获取引用:
83	    → 标记 [CITATION NEEDED] 或 \cite{PLACEHOLDER_verify}
84	    → 明确告知用户
85	    → 绝不编造看似合理的引用
86	```
87	
88	### 3.2 五步验证流程
89	
90	```
91	1. SEARCH  → Semantic Scholar API 搜索关键词
92	2. VERIFY  → 至少 2 个来源确认论文存在（S2 + arXiv/CrossRef）
93	3. RETRIEVE → 通过 DOI 获取 BibTeX（程序化，非记忆）
94	4. CHECK   → 确认你引用的 claim 确实出自该论文
95	5. ADD     → 加入 .bib 文件
96	```
97	
98	### 3.3 API 速查
99	
100	| API | 用途 | 限制 |
101	|-----|------|------|
102	| **Semantic Scholar** | ML/AI 论文搜索 | 1 RPS (免费) |
103	| **CrossRef** | DOI → BibTeX | 需 mailto 头 |
104	| **arXiv** | 预印本搜索 | 3s 间隔 |
105	
106	```python
107	# DOI → BibTeX（最可靠的方式）
108	import requests
109	def doi_to_bibtex(doi: str) -> str:
110	    r = requests.get(f"https://doi.org/{doi}",
111	                     headers={"Accept": "application/x-bibtex"})
112	    r.raise_for_status()
113	    return r.text
114	
115	# Semantic Scholar 搜索
116	from semanticscholar import SemanticScholar
117	sch = SemanticScholar()
118	results = sch.search_paper("attention mechanism transformers", limit=5)
119	for p in results:
120	    print(f"{p.title} | DOI: {p.externalIds.get('DOI', 'N/A')}")
121	```
122	
123	### 3.4 引用处理规则
124	
125	| 情况 | 处理 |
126	|------|------|
127	| 找到论文 + DOI + BibTeX | 直接用 |
128	| 找到论文，无 DOI | 用 arXiv BibTeX |
129	| 论文存在但无法获取 BibTeX | 标记 placeholder，告知用户 |
130	| 不确定论文是否存在 | 标记 `[CITATION NEEDED]`，告知用户 |
131	| "我觉得有篇关于 X 的论文" | **绝不引用** — 先搜索或标记 |
132	
133	---
134	
135	## 4. 顶会模板速查
136	
137	### 4.1 ML/AI 会议
138	
139	| 会议 | 页数限制 | 主文件 | 样式文件 | 必须项 |
140	|------|---------|--------|---------|--------|
141	| **NeurIPS** | 9 页 | `main.tex` | `neurips.sty` | Paper Checklist |
142	| **ICML** | 8 页 (+1 camera-ready) | `example_paper.tex` | `icml2026.sty` | Broader Impact |
143	| **ICLR** | 9 页 (+1) | `iclr_conference.tex` | `iclr_conference.sty` | LLM 使用声明 |
144	| **ACL/EMNLP** | 8 页 (long) | `acl_latex.tex` | `acl.sty` | Limitations 必须 |
145	| **AAAI** | 7 页 (+1) | `aaai_template.tex` | `aaai.sty` | 严格样式 |
146	| **COLM** | 9 页 (+1) | `colm_conference.tex` | `colm_conference.sty` | 语言模型聚焦 |
147	
148	### 4.2 系统会议
149	
150	| 会议 | 页数限制 | 模板类型 | 关键要求 |
151	|------|---------|---------|---------|
152	| **OSDI** | 12 页 (+2) | USENIX `usenix.sty` | Research / Operational 双 track |
153	| **NSDI** | 12 页 | USENIX | Introduction 预筛 |
154	| **ASPLOS** | 12 页 | ACM `acmart.cls (sigplan)` | 前 2 页快速评审 |
155	| **SOSP** | 12 页 | ACM `acmart.cls (sigplan)` | 可选 Artifact Evaluation |
156	
157	### 4.3 模板使用原则
158	
159	```bash
160	# 1. 复制整个模板目录（不要只拷 .tex）
161	cp -r templates/neurips2025/ ~/papers/my-paper/
162	
163	# 2. 先编译未修改的模板，确认能跑通
164	latexmk -pdf main.tex
165	
166	# 3. 逐章替换内容，频繁编译
167	```
168	
169	**禁止事项：**
170	- 不要修改 `.sty` 文件
171	- 不要在会议模板间复制 `\usepackage` 行
172	- 不要只复制 `.tex` 而不带 `.sty/.bst`
173	
174	---
175	
176	## 5. 写作规范
177	
178	### 5.1 时间分配（Neel Nanda）
179	
180	花**大致相等**的时间在：
181	1. Abstract
182	2. Introduction
183	3. 图表
184	4. **其余所有内容加起来**
185	
186	审稿人读论文的顺序：标题 → 摘要 → 引言 → 图表 → 也许正文。
187	
188	### 5.2 Abstract 五句法（Sebastian Farquhar）
189	
190	```
191	1. 你做了什么（"We introduce/prove/demonstrate..."）
192	2. 为什么这很难且重要
193	3. 怎么做的（含专业关键词以便检索）
194	4. 有什么证据
195	5. 最惊人的数字/结果
196	```
197	
198	删除一切泛泛的开头：~~"Large language models have achieved remarkable success..."~~
199	
200	### 5.3 句子级清晰度（Gopen & Swan）
201	
202	| 原则 | 规则 |
203	|------|------|
204	| 主谓紧邻 | 不要在主语和动词之间插入长从句 |
205	| 重点在句尾 | 把关键数字/结论放在句末 |
206	| 旧信息在前 | 先放读者已知的内容，再引入新概念 |
207	| 动词表达动作 | "We analyzed" 而非 "We performed an analysis" |
208	
209	### 5.4 常见修改
210	
211	| 问题 | 修复 |
212	|------|------|
213	| Abstract 太泛 | 删第一句（如果它能放在任何 ML 论文前面） |
214	| Introduction 超 1.5 页 | 背景挪到 Related Work |
215	| 实验没有显式 claim | 每个实验前加 "This tests whether..." |
216	| 缺统计显著性 | 加 error bars + 运行次数 + 计算方法 |
217	
218	---
219	
220	## 6. 投稿工程链
221	
222	### 6.1 构建
223	
224	```bash
225	# 推荐：latexmk 一键构建
226	latexmk -pdf -interaction=nonstopmode -halt-on-error main.tex
227	
228	# 手动：需要多次编译
229	pdflatex main.tex && bibtex main && pdflatex main.tex && pdflatex main.tex
230	```
231	
232	### 6.2 Lint + 格式化
233	
234	```bash
235	# Lint: 检查常见 LaTeX 问题
236	chktex main.tex
237	
238	# 格式化: 减少 diff 噪声
239	latexindent -w main.tex
240	```
241	
242	### 6.3 图表格式
243	
244	| 类型 | 格式 | 说明 |
245	|------|------|------|
246	| 矢量图（plot、diagram） | PDF | matplotlib: `plt.savefig('fig.pdf')` |
247	| 照片/heatmap | PNG 600dpi 或 TIFF | 栅格图 |
248	| 表格 | `booktabs` 包 | `\toprule/\midrule/\bottomrule` |
249	
250	```latex
251	\usepackage{booktabs}
252	\begin{tabular}{lcc}
253	\toprule
254	Method & Accuracy $\uparrow$ & Latency $\downarrow$ \\
255	\midrule
256	Baseline & 85.2 & 45ms \\
257	\textbf{Ours} & \textbf{92.1} & 38ms \\
258	\bottomrule
259	\end{tabular}
260	```
261	
262	**图表规范：**
263	- 用色盲友好色板（Okabe-Ito 或 Paul Tol）
264	- 图内不放标题（用 caption）
265	- Caption 独立可理解（不依赖正文）
266	- 最佳值加粗，标注方向符号（↑ 越高越好，↓ 越低越好）
267	
268	### 6.4 投稿打包
269	
270	```bash
271	# 清理辅助文件
272	latexmk -c
273	
274	# 打包投稿
275	zip -r submission.zip main.tex *.sty *.bst *.bib figures/ --exclude='*.aux' --exclude='*.log'
276	```
277	
278	### 6.5 常见失败点
279	
280	| 问题 | 解决 |
281	|------|------|
282	| 图片格式混用导致编译失败 | 统一用 PDF |
283	| 字体未嵌入 | `pdffonts output.pdf` 检查 |
284	| Overfull box 过多 | 关键位置手动调行 |
285	| 引用缺字段 | 检查 DOI/年份/期刊名 |
286	| 超页数 | 用 `\vspace{-Xpt}` 微调，或精简内容 |
287	
288	---
289	
290	## 7. 会议转投
291	
292	当论文被拒或转投其他会议时：
293	
294	### 7.1 ML/AI 会议间转换
295	
296	| 转换 | 页数变化 | 关键调整 |
297	|------|---------|---------|
298	| NeurIPS → ICML | 9→8 | 删 1 页，加 Broader Impact |
299	| ICML → ICLR | 8→9 | 可扩展实验 + LLM 声明 |
300	| NeurIPS → ACL | 9→8 | 按 NLP 惯例重组 + Limitations |
301	| ICLR → AAAI | 9→7 | 大幅精简，严格样式 |
302	
303	### 7.2 转投原则
304	
305	1. **永远用目标模板重新开始** — 复制目标模板，迁移内容，不要合并 preamble
306	2. **只迁移正文内容** — 不复制 `\usepackage`、header/footer 命令
307	3. **根据审稿意见改进** — 但不要在新稿中提及旧投稿（双盲）
308	4. **检查目标会议特殊要求** — checklist、ethics statement、LLM 声明等
309	
310	---
311	
312	## 8. 投前清单
313	
314	### 通用清单
315	
316	- [ ] Abstract/Intro/Conclusion 的 claim 一致
317	- [ ] 每个 contribution 有对应 evidence
318	- [ ] 所有引用已程序化验证（无幻觉引用）
319	- [ ] Error bars + 运行次数 + 统计方法
320	- [ ] Limitations 章节存在且诚实
321	- [ ] 匿名化（双盲审稿）
322	- [ ] 符合页数限制
323	- [ ] 所有图表有自包含 caption
324	- [ ] `.bib` 中无缺失字段
325	- [ ] PDF 编译无 warning
326	
327	### 会议特定
328	
329	| 会议 | 额外要求 |
330	|------|---------|
331	| NeurIPS | 16 项 Paper Checklist（附录，不计页数） |
332	| ICML | Broader Impact Statement |
333	| ICLR | LLM 使用声明 |
334	| ACL/EMNLP | Limitations 章节（必须），Ethics Statement |
335	| AAAI | 严格样式文件合规 |
336	
337	---
338	
339	## 参考资源
340	
341	**写作方法论：**
342	- [Neel Nanda: How to Write ML Papers](https://www.alignmentforum.org/posts/eJGptPbbFPZGLpjsp/) — What/Why/So What 框架
343	- [Farquhar: How to Write ML Papers](https://sebastianfarquhar.com/on-research/2024/11/04/how_to_write_ml_papers/) — 五句法 Abstract
344	- [Gopen & Swan: Science of Scientific Writing](https://cseweb.ucsd.edu/~swanson/papers/science-of-writing.pdf) — 读者预期 7 原则
345	- [Lipton: Heuristics for Scientific Writing](https://www.approximatelycorrect.com/2018/01/29/heuristics-technical-scientific-writing-machine-learning-perspective/) — 用词
346	- [Perez: Easy Paper Writing Tips](https://ethanperez.net/easy-paper-writing-tips/) — 微观清晰度
347	
348	**API：**
349	- [Semantic Scholar](https://api.semanticscholar.org/api-docs/) | [CrossRef](https://www.crossref.org/documentation/) | [arXiv](https://info.arxiv.org/help/api/)
350	
351	**会议官方：**
352	- [NeurIPS](https://neurips.cc/) | [ICML](https://icml.cc/) | [ICLR](https://iclr.cc/) | [ACL](https://www.aclweb.org/) | [AAAI](https://aaai.org/) | [EMNLP](https://2025.emnlp.org/)

# LaTeX 论文写作全流程

ML/AI 顶会论文从草稿到投稿的完整指南。整合 Orchestra Research、VibeSkills、claim2evidence 三方最佳实践。

---

## 1. 工作模式

开始前选择模式：

| 模式 | 说明 | 适用 |
|------|------|------|
| **Build** | 从实验笔记/结果/代码生成论文 | 新稿 |
| **Improve** | 改写已有章节，强化论证 | 修改稿 |
| **Audit** | 输出风险列表 + 缺失证据 + 修复建议 | 投前检查 |

---

## 2. Claim-Evidence 方法论

**核心原则：论文是一个有中心贡献的故事，不是实验的堆砌。**

### 2.1 一句话贡献

在写任何内容之前，必须能用一句话说清贡献。如果不能，说明还没准备好写论文。

### 2.2 Claim-Evidence Map

为每个 contribution 建立 claim→evidence 映射表：

| Contribution | Claim | Evidence | Table/Figure |
|-------------|-------|----------|-------------|
| C1: 方法 X 在 Y 上 SOTA | 比所有 baseline 高 ≥2% | 5-seed 平均，p<0.05 | Table 1 |
| C2: 消融证明 Z 是关键 | 去掉 Z 后掉 >5% | 消融实验 | Table 2 |
| C3: 计算效率 | 比 baseline 快 3× | FLOPs + wall-clock | Figure 3 |

**没有直接证据支撑的 claim 必须删除或降级为 discussion。**

### 2.3 章节起草顺序

```
1. Introduction + Experiments（先确定 claim 和 evidence）
2. Method（评估问题稳定后再写细节）
3. Related Work
4. Abstract + Title（核心 claim 定型后最后写）
```

### 2.4 Quality Gates

投稿前必须通过：
- [ ] 前两段出现显式 novelty 声明
- [ ] 每个 contribution 有可验证的 evidence
- [ ] Abstract / Intro / Conclusion 的 claim 一致
- [ ] Limitations 真实且技术性诚实
- [ ] 审稿人两分钟内能识别 delta

---

## 3. 引用防幻觉（CRITICAL）

**AI 生成引用有 ~40% 错误率。绝对禁止凭记忆写 BibTeX。**

### 3.1 黄金法则

```
IF 无法程序化获取引用:
    → 标记 [CITATION NEEDED] 或 \cite{PLACEHOLDER_verify}
    → 明确告知用户
    → 绝不编造看似合理的引用
```

### 3.2 五步验证流程

```
1. SEARCH  → Semantic Scholar API 搜索关键词
2. VERIFY  → 至少 2 个来源确认论文存在（S2 + arXiv/CrossRef）
3. RETRIEVE → 通过 DOI 获取 BibTeX（程序化，非记忆）
4. CHECK   → 确认你引用的 claim 确实出自该论文
5. ADD     → 加入 .bib 文件
```

### 3.3 API 速查

| API | 用途 | 限制 |
|-----|------|------|
| **Semantic Scholar** | ML/AI 论文搜索 | 1 RPS (免费) |
| **CrossRef** | DOI → BibTeX | 需 mailto 头 |
| **arXiv** | 预印本搜索 | 3s 间隔 |

```python
# DOI → BibTeX（最可靠的方式）
import requests
def doi_to_bibtex(doi: str) -> str:
    r = requests.get(f"https://doi.org/{doi}",
                     headers={"Accept": "application/x-bibtex"})
    r.raise_for_status()
    return r.text

# Semantic Scholar 搜索
from semanticscholar import SemanticScholar
sch = SemanticScholar()
results = sch.search_paper("attention mechanism transformers", limit=5)
for p in results:
    print(f"{p.title} | DOI: {p.externalIds.get('DOI', 'N/A')}")
```

### 3.4 引用处理规则

| 情况 | 处理 |
|------|------|
| 找到论文 + DOI + BibTeX | 直接用 |
| 找到论文，无 DOI | 用 arXiv BibTeX |
| 论文存在但无法获取 BibTeX | 标记 placeholder，告知用户 |
| 不确定论文是否存在 | 标记 `[CITATION NEEDED]`，告知用户 |
| "我觉得有篇关于 X 的论文" | **绝不引用** — 先搜索或标记 |

---

## 4. 顶会模板速查

### 4.1 ML/AI 会议

| 会议 | 页数限制 | 主文件 | 样式文件 | 必须项 |
|------|---------|--------|---------|--------|
| **NeurIPS** | 9 页 | `main.tex` | `neurips.sty` | Paper Checklist |
| **ICML** | 8 页 (+1 camera-ready) | `example_paper.tex` | `icml2026.sty` | Broader Impact |
| **ICLR** | 9 页 (+1) | `iclr_conference.tex` | `iclr_conference.sty` | LLM 使用声明 |
| **ACL/EMNLP** | 8 页 (long) | `acl_latex.tex` | `acl.sty` | Limitations 必须 |
| **AAAI** | 7 页 (+1) | `aaai_template.tex` | `aaai.sty` | 严格样式 |
| **COLM** | 9 页 (+1) | `colm_conference.tex` | `colm_conference.sty` | 语言模型聚焦 |

### 4.2 系统会议

| 会议 | 页数限制 | 模板类型 | 关键要求 |
|------|---------|---------|---------|
| **OSDI** | 12 页 (+2) | USENIX `usenix.sty` | Research / Operational 双 track |
| **NSDI** | 12 页 | USENIX | Introduction 预筛 |
| **ASPLOS** | 12 页 | ACM `acmart.cls (sigplan)` | 前 2 页快速评审 |
| **SOSP** | 12 页 | ACM `acmart.cls (sigplan)` | 可选 Artifact Evaluation |

### 4.3 模板使用原则

```bash
# 1. 复制整个模板目录（不要只拷 .tex）
cp -r templates/neurips2025/ ~/papers/my-paper/

# 2. 先编译未修改的模板，确认能跑通
latexmk -pdf main.tex

# 3. 逐章替换内容，频繁编译
```

**禁止事项：**
- 不要修改 `.sty` 文件
- 不要在会议模板间复制 `\usepackage` 行
- 不要只复制 `.tex` 而不带 `.sty/.bst`

---

## 5. 写作规范

### 5.1 时间分配（Neel Nanda）

花**大致相等**的时间在：
1. Abstract
2. Introduction
3. 图表
4. **其余所有内容加起来**

审稿人读论文的顺序：标题 → 摘要 → 引言 → 图表 → 也许正文。

### 5.2 Abstract 五句法（Sebastian Farquhar）

```
1. 你做了什么（"We introduce/prove/demonstrate..."）
2. 为什么这很难且重要
3. 怎么做的（含专业关键词以便检索）
4. 有什么证据
5. 最惊人的数字/结果
```

删除一切泛泛的开头：~~"Large language models have achieved remarkable success..."~~

### 5.3 句子级清晰度（Gopen & Swan）

| 原则 | 规则 |
|------|------|
| 主谓紧邻 | 不要在主语和动词之间插入长从句 |
| 重点在句尾 | 把关键数字/结论放在句末 |
| 旧信息在前 | 先放读者已知的内容，再引入新概念 |
| 动词表达动作 | "We analyzed" 而非 "We performed an analysis" |

### 5.4 常见修改

| 问题 | 修复 |
|------|------|
| Abstract 太泛 | 删第一句（如果它能放在任何 ML 论文前面） |
| Introduction 超 1.5 页 | 背景挪到 Related Work |
| 实验没有显式 claim | 每个实验前加 "This tests whether..." |
| 缺统计显著性 | 加 error bars + 运行次数 + 计算方法 |

---

## 6. 投稿工程链

### 6.1 构建

```bash
# 推荐：latexmk 一键构建
latexmk -pdf -interaction=nonstopmode -halt-on-error main.tex

# 手动：需要多次编译
pdflatex main.tex && bibtex main && pdflatex main.tex && pdflatex main.tex
```

### 6.2 Lint + 格式化

```bash
# Lint: 检查常见 LaTeX 问题
chktex main.tex

# 格式化: 减少 diff 噪声
latexindent -w main.tex
```

### 6.3 图表格式

| 类型 | 格式 | 说明 |
|------|------|------|
| 矢量图（plot、diagram） | PDF | matplotlib: `plt.savefig('fig.pdf')` |
| 照片/heatmap | PNG 600dpi 或 TIFF | 栅格图 |
| 表格 | `booktabs` 包 | `\toprule/\midrule/\bottomrule` |

```latex
\usepackage{booktabs}
\begin{tabular}{lcc}
\toprule
Method & Accuracy $\uparrow$ & Latency $\downarrow$ \\
\midrule
Baseline & 85.2 & 45ms \\
\textbf{Ours} & \textbf{92.1} & 38ms \\
\bottomrule
\end{tabular}
```

**图表规范：**
- 用色盲友好色板（Okabe-Ito 或 Paul Tol）
- 图内不放标题（用 caption）
- Caption 独立可理解（不依赖正文）
- 最佳值加粗，标注方向符号（↑ 越高越好，↓ 越低越好）

### 6.4 投稿打包

```bash
# 清理辅助文件
latexmk -c

# 打包投稿
zip -r submission.zip main.tex *.sty *.bst *.bib figures/ --exclude='*.aux' --exclude='*.log'
```

### 6.5 常见失败点

| 问题 | 解决 |
|------|------|
| 图片格式混用导致编译失败 | 统一用 PDF |
| 字体未嵌入 | `pdffonts output.pdf` 检查 |
| Overfull box 过多 | 关键位置手动调行 |
| 引用缺字段 | 检查 DOI/年份/期刊名 |
| 超页数 | 用 `\vspace{-Xpt}` 微调，或精简内容 |

---

## 7. 会议转投

当论文被拒或转投其他会议时：

### 7.1 ML/AI 会议间转换

| 转换 | 页数变化 | 关键调整 |
|------|---------|---------|
| NeurIPS → ICML | 9→8 | 删 1 页，加 Broader Impact |
| ICML → ICLR | 8→9 | 可扩展实验 + LLM 声明 |
| NeurIPS → ACL | 9→8 | 按 NLP 惯例重组 + Limitations |
| ICLR → AAAI | 9→7 | 大幅精简，严格样式 |

### 7.2 转投原则

1. **永远用目标模板重新开始** — 复制目标模板，迁移内容，不要合并 preamble
2. **只迁移正文内容** — 不复制 `\usepackage`、header/footer 命令
3. **根据审稿意见改进** — 但不要在新稿中提及旧投稿（双盲）
4. **检查目标会议特殊要求** — checklist、ethics statement、LLM 声明等

---

## 8. 投前清单

### 通用清单

- [ ] Abstract/Intro/Conclusion 的 claim 一致
- [ ] 每个 contribution 有对应 evidence
- [ ] 所有引用已程序化验证（无幻觉引用）
- [ ] Error bars + 运行次数 + 统计方法
- [ ] Limitations 章节存在且诚实
- [ ] 匿名化（双盲审稿）
- [ ] 符合页数限制
- [ ] 所有图表有自包含 caption
- [ ] `.bib` 中无缺失字段
- [ ] PDF 编译无 warning

### 会议特定

| 会议 | 额外要求 |
|------|---------|
| NeurIPS | 16 项 Paper Checklist（附录，不计页数） |
| ICML | Broader Impact Statement |
| ICLR | LLM 使用声明 |
| ACL/EMNLP | Limitations 章节（必须），Ethics Statement |
| AAAI | 严格样式文件合规 |

---

\section{Introduction}
\label{sec:introduction}

Vision-language-action models (VLAs) achieve strong manipulation performance by fine-tuning large language models on robot demonstration data~\cite{brohan2023_rt2,kim2024_openvla}.
The prevailing architectural assumption is that LLM fine-tuning injects action-relevant representational knowledge into the system---that the language backbone learns to transform visual input into representations suited for action prediction.
Yet this assumption has not been tested at the representational level.
Where do the representations that drive action prediction actually originate?
The answer has direct consequences for VLA design: if the LLM backbone is the primary source of action structure, scaling and training the LLM is the critical lever; if instead the pretrained vision encoder already supplies this structure, investment should prioritize visual representation quality.

Recent work has begun to probe this question from complementary angles.
At the behavioral level, \cite{grant2026} demonstrated that VLA policies are disproportionately driven by visual input, with language instructions having limited influence on action selection.
Representational analyses of VLA internals further suggest that language instructions are largely ignored by the action generation pathway~\cite{haon2025}.
However, these studies operate at the behavioral or single-component level---none has performed a systematic \emph{representational decomposition} that quantifies how each architectural component (vision encoder, projector, LLM layers) independently contributes to action-relevant structure.
Without such a decomposition, it remains unclear whether VLA fine-tuning creates new action knowledge or merely reconfigures structure inherited from pretrained components.

We address this gap by decomposing OpenVLA-7B~\cite{kim2024_openvla,karamcheti2024}, a VLA that chains a frozen SigLIP vision encoder~\cite{zhai2023_siglip}, an MLP projector, and a Llama-2 7B language backbone fine-tuned on LIBERO-10~\cite{liu2023_libero}.
We extract representations from the projector output, each of the 32 LLM layers at both distributed image-token and readout-token positions, and two external baselines---CLIP ViT-L/14~\cite{radford2021_clip} and DINOv2 ViT-L/14~\cite{oquab2024_dinov2}---that isolate the effect of pretraining objective (vision-language vs.\ vision-only).
To disentangle training from architecture, we cross two factors in a $2 \times 2$ factorial design: LLM training status (trained vs.\ untrained, with the untrained control reinitializing all 6.74B LLM parameters) and instruction presence (with vs.\ without language instruction).
We quantify action-relevant structure using Representational Similarity Analysis (RSA)~\cite{kriegeskorte2008}, which measures geometric alignment between representations and the action space, and functional MLP probes~\cite{alain2017}, which measure decodability of action vectors from frozen representations.

Three findings emerge from this decomposition.
\emph{First}, the frozen vision-language encoder provides the dominant source of action-relevant geometric structure.
SigLIP+Projector achieves the highest action-space alignment (RSA $\rho = 0.615$); CLIP, an independent VL-pretrained encoder with no VLA training signal, achieves $\rho = 0.557$---both far exceeding vision-only DINOv2 ($\rho = 0.388$).
This 0.169-point gap between CLIP and DINOv2, two ViT-L/14 architectures differing primarily in pretraining objective, isolates VL pretraining as the operative factor.
The LLM never exceeds $\rho = 0.501$ at any layer.
\emph{Second}, the LLM degrades distributed geometric structure ($\rho$: $0.615 \to 0.501$) but concentrates a functionally superior representation at the readout token (probe $R^2 = 0.731$ vs.\ $0.706$ for the projector, $p = 0.001$), characterizing the LLM as an information \emph{router} rather than a knowledge source.
\emph{Third}, the geometric structure is invariant to LLM training ($\Delta\rho = 0.021$, $p = 0.20$, n.s.), while functional concentration at the readout requires it ($\Delta R^2 = 0.045$, $p < 0.0001$).
Training teaches routing, not representation creation.

These findings make three contributions:
\begin{itemize}[nosep,leftmargin=*]
  \item We provide the first representational decomposition of a VLA, separately quantifying the action-relevant structure contributed by the vision encoder, projector, and LLM layers using both geometric (RSA) and functional (probe $R^2$) metrics.
  \item We demonstrate that VL-pretrained vision encoders---not LLM fine-tuning---are the primary source of action-relevant geometric structure, with two independent VL encoders (SigLIP, CLIP) both substantially exceeding vision-only DINOv2.
  \item We characterize the LLM as an information router that concentrates pre-existing vision-encoder geometry at the readout token for action decoding, with training teaching the routing policy rather than creating new representations.
\end{itemize}
These results suggest that vision encoder pretraining quality---specifically, vision-language alignment---is the primary lever for action representations in current VLA architectures, and that the LLM backbone's role is information routing rather than knowledge injection (\S\ref{sec:discussion}).

1	\section{Discussion}
2	\label{sec:discussion}
3	
4	\paragraph{Synthesis.}
5	Our experiments reveal a coherent picture of how action-relevant structure flows through a VLA.
6	The vision encoder is the \emph{source}: VL-pretrained encoders provide geometric structure aligned with the action space (SigLIP+Projector RSA $\rho = 0.615$; CLIP $\rho = 0.557$), far exceeding what the LLM produces at any layer ($\rho \leq 0.501$).
7	The LLM is a \emph{router}: it degrades distributed geometric structure ($\rho$: $0.615 \to 0.501$; $R^2$: $0.706 \to 0.683$) while concentrating a functionally superior representation at the readout token ($R^2 = 0.731$).
8	Training teaches the \emph{routing policy}: the geometric structure itself is invariant to training ($\Delta\rho = 0.021$, $p = 0.20$), but functional concentration at the readout requires it ($\Delta R^2 = 0.045$, $p < 0.0001$).
9	Notably, the projector alone captures 96.6\% of the trained readout's functional capacity ($0.706/0.731$), suggesting that the LLM's contribution, while statistically significant, is incremental.
10	
11	\paragraph{VL pretraining as a general source of action-relevant geometry.}
12	The inclusion of CLIP ViT-L/14 as an external baseline provides evidence that action-relevant geometric structure is a general product of vision-language pretraining, not an artifact of SigLIP's specific architecture or training data.
13	Both VL-pretrained encoders---SigLIP ($\rho = 0.615$) and CLIP ($\rho = 0.557$)---substantially exceed vision-only DINOv2 ($\rho = 0.388$).
14	The 0.169-point gap between CLIP and DINOv2, both ViT-L/14 architectures differing primarily in pretraining objective, isolates language grounding as the operative factor.
15	The additional increment from CLIP to SigLIP+Projector ($\Delta = 0.058$) is consistent with the projector's VLA-supervised alignment providing a modest boost, but the dominant contribution ($\rho = 0.557 \gg 0.388$) originates in VL pretraining itself.
16	
17	\paragraph{Geometric-functional dissociation.}
18	A recurring finding across our analyses is the dissociation between geometric alignment (RSA) and functional decodability (probe $R^2$).
19	DINOv2 achieves probe performance statistically indistinguishable from the SigLIP+Projector ($R^2$: $0.712$ vs.\ $0.706$, $p = 0.22$) despite substantially lower RSA ($0.388$ vs.\ $0.615$).
20	This dissociation implies that action information---in the sense of decodable content---is broadly available in strong visual features regardless of pretraining objective; what VL pretraining adds is \emph{geometric alignment}, organizing that information into a structure that mirrors the action space.
21	For VLA design, this distinction matters: encoder selection determines not just what information is available, but how it is organized, with downstream consequences for how easily the LLM can route it.
22	
23	\paragraph{Metric sensitivity: RSA versus CKA.}
24	The divergence between RSA and linear CKA underscores the importance of multi-metric evaluation.
25	Linear CKA produces a ranking---untrained LLM ($0.089$) $>$ trained ($0.083$) $>$ SigLIP+Projector ($0.081$) $>$ DINOv2 ($0.066$)---that partially reverses the RSA ordering.
26	Under linear CKA, training appears to \emph{reduce} similarity to the action space, an interpretation that contradicts both RSA and functional probe evidence.
27	RDM kernel CKA resolves this discrepancy, restoring the RSA-consistent ranking (trained $0.260$ $>$ Proj $0.257$ $>$ untrained $0.246$ $>$ DINOv2 $0.241$).
28	The divergence likely reflects linear CKA's sensitivity to second-order statistics and its known vulnerability to dimension mismatch between high-dimensional representations and the 7-D action space~\cite{kornblith2019}.
29	The practical implication is that the LLM transforms rather than destroys action structure, but the narrative one draws depends critically on which metric is employed.
30	
31	\paragraph{Implications for VLA design.}
32	Our findings suggest four practical considerations.
33	\emph{First}, vision encoder pretraining quality is the primary lever for action-relevant representations; investing in stronger VL encoders may yield larger gains than scaling the LLM backbone.
34	\emph{Second}, for downstream modules that operate on distributed representations (e.g., auxiliary losses, multi-task heads), the projector output may be preferable to LLM-processed features, given its higher geometric fidelity and 96.6\% of readout-level decodability.
35	\emph{Third}, the LLM's value lies in readout concentration---routing distributed information to a single decoding site---which informs action head design: architectures that exploit this concentration (e.g., reading from a dedicated token rather than pooling LLM features) may better leverage the LLM's trained routing.

38	\paragraph{Connection to behavioral evidence.}

45	We study a single VLA architecture (OpenVLA-7B) on a single benchmark suite (LIBERO); generalization to other architectures (e.g., RT-2~\cite{brohan2023_rt2}) and domains (e.g., mobile manipulation, dexterous hands) remains to be established.

\section{Discussion}
\label{sec:discussion}

\paragraph{Synthesis.}
Our experiments reveal a coherent picture of how action-relevant structure flows through a VLA.
The vision encoder is the \emph{source}: VL-pretrained encoders provide geometric structure aligned with the action space (SigLIP+Projector RSA $\rho = 0.615$; CLIP $\rho = 0.557$), far exceeding what the LLM produces at any layer ($\rho \leq 0.501$).
The LLM is a \emph{router}: it degrades distributed geometric structure ($\rho$: $0.615 \to 0.501$; $R^2$: $0.706 \to 0.683$) while concentrating a functionally superior representation at the readout token ($R^2 = 0.731$).
Training teaches the \emph{routing policy}: the geometric structure itself is invariant to training ($\Delta\rho = 0.021$, $p = 0.20$), but functional concentration at the readout requires it ($\Delta R^2 = 0.045$, $p < 0.0001$).
Notably, the projector alone captures 96.6\% of the trained readout's functional capacity ($0.706/0.731$), suggesting that the LLM's contribution, while statistically significant, is incremental.

\paragraph{VL pretraining as a general source of action-relevant geometry.}
The inclusion of CLIP ViT-L/14 as an external baseline provides evidence that action-relevant geometric structure is a general product of vision-language pretraining, not an artifact of SigLIP's specific architecture or training data.
Both VL-pretrained encoders---SigLIP ($\rho = 0.615$) and CLIP ($\rho = 0.557$)---substantially exceed vision-only DINOv2 ($\rho = 0.388$).
The 0.169-point gap between CLIP and DINOv2, both ViT-L/14 architectures differing primarily in pretraining objective, isolates language grounding as the operative factor.
The additional increment from CLIP to SigLIP+Projector ($\Delta = 0.058$) is consistent with the projector's VLA-supervised alignment providing a modest boost, but the dominant contribution ($\rho = 0.557 \gg 0.388$) originates in VL pretraining itself.

\paragraph{Geometric-functional dissociation.}
A recurring finding across our analyses is the dissociation between geometric alignment (RSA) and functional decodability (probe $R^2$).
DINOv2 achieves probe performance statistically indistinguishable from the SigLIP+Projector ($R^2$: $0.712$ vs.\ $0.706$, $p = 0.22$) despite substantially lower RSA ($0.388$ vs.\ $0.615$).
This dissociation implies that action information---in the sense of decodable content---is broadly available in strong visual features regardless of pretraining objective; what VL pretraining adds is \emph{geometric alignment}, organizing that information into a structure that mirrors the action space.
For VLA design, this distinction matters: encoder selection determines not just what information is available, but how it is organized, with downstream consequences for how easily the LLM can route it.

\paragraph{Metric sensitivity: RSA versus CKA.}
The divergence between RSA and linear CKA underscores the importance of multi-metric evaluation.
Linear CKA produces a ranking---untrained LLM ($0.089$) $>$ trained ($0.083$) $>$ SigLIP+Projector ($0.081$) $>$ DINOv2 ($0.066$)---that partially reverses the RSA ordering.
Under linear CKA, training appears to \emph{reduce} similarity to the action space, an interpretation that contradicts both RSA and functional probe evidence.
RDM kernel CKA resolves this discrepancy, restoring the RSA-consistent ranking (trained $0.260$ $>$ Proj $0.257$ $>$ untrained $0.246$ $>$ DINOv2 $0.241$).
The divergence likely reflects linear CKA's sensitivity to second-order statistics and its known vulnerability to dimension mismatch between high-dimensional representations and the 7-D action space~\cite{kornblith2019}.
The practical implication is that the LLM transforms rather than destroys action structure, but the narrative one draws depends critically on which metric is employed.

\paragraph{Implications for VLA design.}
Our findings suggest four practical considerations.
\emph{First}, vision encoder pretraining quality is the primary lever for action-relevant representations; investing in stronger VL encoders may yield larger gains than scaling the LLM backbone.
\emph{Second}, for downstream modules that operate on distributed representations (e.g., auxiliary losses, multi-task heads), the projector output may be preferable to LLM-processed features, given its higher geometric fidelity and 96.6\% of readout-level decodability.
\emph{Third}, the LLM's value lies in readout concentration---routing distributed information to a single decoding site---which informs action head design: architectures that exploit this concentration (e.g., reading from a dedicated token rather than pooling LLM features) may better leverage the LLM's trained routing.
\emph{Fourth}, the invariance of representation geometry to language instructions ($\Delta\rho = 0.004$, n.s.; content controls within $\pm 0.017$) suggests that instructions influence action selection through a mechanism other than modulating visual representation structure, inviting further investigation into how language conditions behavior in VLAs.

\paragraph{Connection to behavioral evidence.}
Our representational findings complement the behavioral results of \cite{grant2026}, who showed that VLA policies are disproportionately driven by visual input and that language instructions are ``encoded but not used'' for action selection.
Our data provide a representational account of these behavioral patterns: vision dominates because the frozen encoder supplies the action-relevant geometric structure that the LLM routes to the readout, while instruction content does not modulate this geometric structure (all four instruction conditions yield RSA within $\pm 0.017$).
The alignment between representational and behavioral evidence strengthens the case that VL-pretrained vision encoders, rather than LLM reasoning, are the primary computational substrate for action generation in current VLA architectures.

\paragraph{Limitations.}
Several limitations scope our conclusions.
We study a single VLA architecture (OpenVLA-7B) on a single benchmark suite (LIBERO); generalization to other architectures (e.g., RT-2~\cite{brohan2023_rt2}) and domains (e.g., mobile manipulation, dexterous hands) remains to be established.
RSA captures structural alignment between representations and actions but does not establish causal contribution---high RSA does not guarantee that the representation is causally used by the policy.
The CLIP and DINOv2 action probes were trained with different hyperparameters (100 epochs) than the projector and LLM probes (50 epochs); while within-experiment comparisons are valid, absolute $R^2$ values are not directly comparable across these two probe sets, and we have been careful to restrict cross-experiment claims accordingly.
Finally, our analyses characterize frozen representations post hoc; they do not address how these representations emerge during VLA pretraining or fine-tuning, nor whether architectural interventions (e.g., unfreezing the vision encoder) would alter the source--router dynamic we observe.

papers:
  # ============================================================
  # DIRECT COMPETITORS — VLA Representation Analysis / Interpretability
  # ============================================================
  - id: grant2026
    title: "Not All Features Are Created Equal: A Mechanistic Study of Vision-Language-Action Models"
    authors: "Bryce Grant, Xijia Zhao, Peng Wang"
    year: 2026
    venue: "arXiv preprint (under review)"
    arxiv_id: "2603.19233"
    category: direct-competitor
    role: competitor
    key_findings: >
      Visual pathway dominates action generation across all 6 tested VLA architectures (80M–7B params, 394K+ rollout episodes, 4 benchmarks).
      Language sensitivity depends on task structure: when visual context uniquely specifies the task, language is IGNORED;
      when multiple goals share a scene, language becomes essential ("encoded but not used").
      Cross-task activation injection steers robots toward source-task positions (99.8% trajectory alignment with source in X-VLA).
      Multi-pathway architectures (pi0.5, SmolVLA, GR00T) separate motor programs (expert pathway) from goal semantics (VLM pathway).
    relevance_to_us: >
      Most direct competitor. Behavioral intervention (activation injection, SAE, probing) reveals vision dominance + language encoded but not used.
      Uses OpenVLA-OFT checkpoint; we use standard fine-tuning — must qualify this difference in Related Work.
    novelty_gap: >
      No trained vs untrained representation analysis. They compare different model architectures,
      we compare trained vs untrained representation structure within the same architecture.
      Their "encoded but not used" is a behavioral-level conclusion; we demonstrate at the representation level
      that instruction conditioning comes from the input pathway, not training. Complementary work.
    notes: >
      Action Atlas interactive exploration tool released. 6 models: OpenVLA, X-VLA, pi0.5, SmolVLA, GR00T, Octo.
      OFT checkpoint difference may affect direct comparability.

  - id: swann2026
    title: "Sparse Autoencoders Reveal Interpretable and Steerable Features in VLA Models"
    authors: "Aiden Swann, Lachlain McGranahan, Hugo Buurmeijer, Monroe Kennedy III, Mac Schwager"
    year: 2026
    venue: "arXiv preprint"
    arxiv_id: "2603.19183"
    category: direct-competitor
    role: competitor
    key_findings: >
      SAE features on OpenVLA: majority of extracted features correspond to memorized training sequences,
      but some correspond to interpretable, general, and steerable motion primitives and semantic properties.
    relevance_to_us: >
      Also OpenVLA interpretability work. They use SAE for feature-level decomposition,
      we use probing + RSA for representation-level analysis. Methodologically complementary.
    novelty_gap: >
      No language features analysis. No trained vs untrained comparison.
      Does not investigate source of instruction conditioning (input pathway vs training).
    notes: "Stanford team. Published on arXiv same day as Grant 2026 (2026-03-19)."

  - id: rizzardo2026
    title: "Observing and Controlling Features in Vision-Language-Action Models"
    authors: "Rizzardo et al."
    year: 2026
    venue: "arXiv preprint"
    arxiv_id: "2603.05487"
    category: direct-competitor
    role: competitor
    key_findings: >
      Introduces feature-observability and feature-controllability concepts bridging LLM mechanistic
      interpretability and VLAs. Linear classifier observation + optimal-control-based minimal intervention steering.
      Validated on pi0.5 and OpenVLA — targeted interventions steer robot behavior while preserving closed-loop capabilities.
    relevance_to_us: >
      Also VLA internal representation analysis. They focus on how to steer,
      we focus on where conditioning comes from (input pathway vs training).
    novelty_gap: >
      No trained vs untrained comparison. No instruction pathway vs training separation analysis.
      Focuses on controllability rather than representation structure origin.
    notes: "Submitted 2026-03-05."

  - id: haon2025
    title: "Mechanistic Interpretability for Steering Vision-Language-Action Models"
    authors: "Bear Haon, Kaylene Stocking, Ian Chuang, Claire Tomlin"
    year: 2025
    venue: "CoRL 2025"
    arxiv_id: "2509.00328"
    category: direct-competitor
    role: methodology
    key_findings: >
      First VLA mechanistic interpretability framework. Projects feedforward activations onto token embedding basis,
      identifies sparse semantic directions (speed, direction) causally linked to action selection.
      Activation steering modulates behavior in real time without fine-tuning.
      Validated on Pi0 and OpenVLA in LIBERO (simulation) and UR5 (real robot).
    relevance_to_us: >
      Methodological reference: their activation steering proves VLAs have interpretable semantic directions.
      Our RSA/probing results can dialogue with their mechanistic findings.
    novelty_gap: >
      No trained vs untrained comparison. No systematic representation structure analysis (RSA/CKA).
      Focuses on individual semantic direction causal intervention, not overall structure comparison.
    notes: "CoRL 2025 accepted. Pioneering work in VLA interpretability."

  - id: molinari2025
    title: "Emergent World Representations in OpenVLA"
    authors: "Marco Molinari, Leonardo Nevali, Saharsha Navani, Omar G. Younis"
    year: 2025
    venue: "arXiv preprint"
    arxiv_id: "2509.24559"
    category: direct-competitor
    role: context
    key_findings: >
      OpenVLA implicitly learns a world model. Embedding arithmetic tests state transition knowledge;
      linear/non-linear probes show statistically significant state transition prediction ability across layers.
      SAE pipeline analyzes fine-grained world model structure.
    relevance_to_us: >
      Also OpenVLA probing work. They study world model, we study instruction conditioning.
      Their layer-wise probe results can be compared with our layer-wise RSA.
    novelty_gap: >
      No language/instruction analysis. No trained vs untrained comparison.
      Only focuses on state transitions, not goal/instruction representation.
    notes: "Submitted 2025-09-29. Has OpenReview discussion."

  - id: lu2025
    title: "Probing a Vision-Language-Action Model for Symbolic States and Integration into a Cognitive Architecture"
    authors: "Hong Lu, Hengxu Li, Prithviraj Singh Shahani, Stephanie Herbers, Matthias Scheutz"
    year: 2025
    venue: "arXiv preprint"
    arxiv_id: "2502.04558"
    category: direct-competitor
    role: methodology
    key_findings: >
      Probes OpenVLA hidden layers to extract symbolic representations (object properties, relations, action states).
      LIBERO-spatial pick-and-place probing accuracy > 0.90 across most layers.
      Integration with cognitive architecture improves interpretability and robustness.
    relevance_to_us: >
      Directly related methodology: both use linear probes on OpenVLA layers on LIBERO.
      Their finding that symbolic states are decodable (>0.90) is consistent with our goal classification at 100%.
    novelty_gap: >
      Only trained model probing, no untrained control.
      Only LIBERO-spatial single task, no cross-task/cross-condition analysis.
      No instruction conditioning source analysis.
    notes: "Submitted 2025-02-06. Tufts University."

  - id: fang_intention2025
    title: "From Intention to Execution: Probing the Generalization Boundaries of Vision-Language-Action Models"
    authors: "Irving Fang, Juexiao Zhang, Shengbang Tong, Chen Feng"
    year: 2025
    venue: "arXiv preprint"
    arxiv_id: "2506.09930"
    category: direct-competitor
    role: context
    key_findings: >
      Unified probing suite (50 simulation tasks, 10 subcategories) evaluating VLA generalization boundaries.
      VLM backbone provides robust perceptual understanding + high-level planning (good intentions),
      but cannot reliably translate to precise motor execution (perception-to-action gap).
      Action data fine-tuning erodes original VLM generalist reasoning abilities.
    relevance_to_us: >
      "Fine-tuning erodes VLM reasoning" echoes our "training doesn't improve representation" finding.
      They discover intention != execution at behavioral level; we discover
      training ~= untrained in representation structure.
    novelty_gap: >
      Behavioral-level probing (success rates), not representation-level analysis.
      No trained vs untrained representation structure comparison.
    notes: "Submitted 2025-06-11. INT-ACT benchmark open-sourced. NYU/ai4ce team."

  # ============================================================
  # DIRECT COMPETITORS — Language Grounding / Counterfactual
  # ============================================================
  - id: fang_cf2026
    title: "When Vision Overrides Language: Evaluating and Mitigating Counterfactual Failures in VLAs"
    authors: "Yu Fang, Yuchun Feng, Dong Jing, Jiaqi Liu, Yue Yang, Zhenyu Wei, Daniel Szafir, Mingyu Ding"
    year: 2026
    venue: "arXiv preprint"
    arxiv_id: "2602.17659"
    category: direct-competitor
    role: competitor
    key_findings: >
      Introduces LIBERO-CF counterfactual benchmark. VLAs exhibit severe counterfactual failures:
      vision shortcuts + dataset biases cause models to ignore language intent.
      OpenVLA-OFT: 4.7% grounding rate, 0.4% success rate.
      Best model: 30.8% grounding rate, 13.2% success rate.
      Proposes Counterfactual Action Guidance (CAG) dual-branch inference scheme.
    relevance_to_us: >
      Directly validates "language encoded but not used" severity under counterfactual settings.
      Their behavioral findings complement our representation-level findings.
      They test OpenVLA-OFT — same checkpoint issue as Grant 2026.
    novelty_gap: >
      Pure behavioral benchmark, no representation analysis.
      No trained vs untrained comparison. No instruction pathway causal analysis.
    notes: "Submitted 2026-02-19. LIBERO-CF has 4 sub-suites (CF-Spatial, CF-Object, CF-Long, CF-OOD)."

  - id: hou2026
    title: "LangGap: Diagnosing and Closing the Language Gap in Vision-Language-Action Models"
    authors: "Yuchen Hou, Lin Zhao"
    year: 2026
    venue: "arXiv preprint"
    arxiv_id: "2603.00592"
    category: direct-competitor
    role: context
    key_findings: >
      SOTA VLAs achieve >95% on standard benchmarks but largely ignore language instructions.
      Four-dimensional semantic perturbation method exposes language understanding deficits.
      LIBERO assigns only 1 task per layout, so models dont need to understand language.
      LangGap benchmark forces multi-task shared layouts; data augmentation improves from 0% to 90%.
    relevance_to_us: >
      Systematic diagnosis of "VLAs ignore language" supports our story:
      instruction conditioning comes from input pathway, not training — even trained VLAs dont truly leverage language.
    novelty_gap: >
      Behavioral-level diagnosis + data augmentation solution. No representation analysis.
      No trained vs untrained comparison. No input pathway causal analysis.
    notes: "Submitted 2026-02-28. GitHub open-sourced."

  # ============================================================
  # METHOD COMPONENT — RSA, CKA, Linear Probing
  # ============================================================
  - id: kriegeskorte2008
    title: "Representational Similarity Analysis - Connecting the Branches of Systems Neuroscience"
    authors: "Nikolaus Kriegeskorte, Marieke Mur, Peter Bandettini"
    year: 2008
    venue: "Frontiers in Systems Neuroscience"
    arxiv_id: null
    doi: "10.3389/neuro.06.004.2008"
    category: method-component
    role: methodology
    key_findings: >
      Introduces Representational Dissimilarity Matrix (RDM) framework for comparing multi-channel
      neural activity measurements with computational models and behavior.
      Validated on fMRI visual cortex data.
    relevance_to_us: "RSA is one of our core analysis methods for comparing trained/untrained/DINO representation structures."
    novelty_gap: null
    notes: "Original RSA paper. 5000+ citations."

  - id: kornblith2019
    title: "Similarity of Neural Network Representations Revisited"
    authors: "Simon Kornblith, Mohammad Norouzi, Honglak Lee, Geoffrey Hinton"
    year: 2019
    venue: "ICML 2019"
    arxiv_id: "1905.00414"
    category: method-component
    role: methodology
    key_findings: >
      Introduces Centered Kernel Alignment (CKA) as representation similarity metric.
      CKA reliably identifies representation correspondences across differently initialized networks,
      outperforming CCA-based methods.
    relevance_to_us: >
      CKA is one of our core tools for comparing trained vs untrained representations.
      Deep-layer CKA reaching 0.86 demonstrates high representation similarity.
    novelty_gap: null
    notes: "Google Brain. CKA is now standard for representation comparison."

  - id: alain2017
    title: "Understanding Intermediate Layers Using Linear Classifier Probes"
    authors: "Guillaume Alain, Yoshua Bengio"
    year: 2017
    venue: "ICLR 2017 Workshop"
    arxiv_id: "1610.01644"
    category: method-component
    role: methodology
    key_findings: >
      Proposes linear classifier probes to monitor feature suitability for classification at every layer.
      Linear separability increases monotonically along network depth.
      Validated on Inception v3 and ResNet-50.
    relevance_to_us: "Linear probing is the methodological foundation for our goal classification and action prediction experiments."
    novelty_gap: null
    notes: "Foundational probing methodology work."

  # ============================================================
  # VISION ENCODERS — SigLIP, DINOv2, CLIP
  # ============================================================
  - id: zhai2023_siglip
    title: "Sigmoid Loss for Language Image Pre-Training"
    authors: "Xiaohua Zhai, Basil Mustafa, Alexander Kolesnikov, Lucas Beyer"
    year: 2023
    venue: "ICCV 2023"
    arxiv_id: "2303.15343"
    category: vision-encoder
    role: baseline
    verified: true
    key_findings: >
      Replaces softmax contrastive loss with pairwise sigmoid loss for VL pretraining.
      Eliminates global batch normalization, enabling smaller batch training.
      SigLIP-SO400M achieves competitive zero-shot performance with simpler training.
    relevance_to_us: >
      SigLIP-SO400M is OpenVLA's frozen vision encoder. Our RSA=0.615 for SigLIP+Projector
      shows this encoder provides dominant action-relevant geometric structure.
    novelty_gap: null
    notes: "Google. OpenVLA uses SigLIP-SO400M/14 variant."

  - id: oquab2024_dinov2
    title: "DINOv2: Learning Robust Visual Features without Supervision"
    authors: "Maxime Oquab, Timothée Darcet, Théo Moutakanni, et al."
    year: 2024
    venue: "TMLR 2024"
    arxiv_id: "2304.07193"
    category: vision-encoder
    role: baseline
    verified: true
    key_findings: >
      Self-supervised ViT trained on curated 142M image dataset (LVD-142M).
      Produces general-purpose features competitive with task-specific models.
      No language supervision — purely vision self-supervised.
    relevance_to_us: >
      Vision-only baseline in our analysis. DINO RSA=0.388 << SigLIP 0.615,
      but DINO R²=0.712 ≈ Projector R²=0.706 — key geometric-functional dissociation.
    novelty_gap: null
    notes: "Meta AI. DINOv2 ViT-L/14 used as vision-only control."

  - id: radford2021_clip
    title: "Learning Transferable Visual Models From Natural Language Supervision"
    authors: "Alec Radford, Jong Wook Kim, Chris Hallacy, et al."
    year: 2021
    venue: "ICML 2021"
    arxiv_id: "2103.00020"
    category: vision-encoder
    role: baseline
    verified: true
    key_findings: >
      Contrastive language-image pretraining on 400M image-text pairs.
      Zero-shot transfer competitive with supervised baselines.
      Pioneering VL pretraining approach.
    relevance_to_us: >

\section{Related Work}\label{sec:related_work}

\paragraph{Vision-language-action models.}
VLAs fine-tune large language models on robot demonstration data to produce action-conditioned policies.
RT-2~\cite{brohan2023_rt2} pioneered this paradigm by co-fine-tuning PaLM-E on robotic trajectories; OpenVLA~\cite{kim2024_openvla} extended it with open-source weights and 970K demonstrations, built on the Prismatic VLM architecture~\cite{karamcheti2024} that chains frozen vision encoders with a Llama-2 backbone.
These architectures share a core design assumption---that LLM fine-tuning injects action-relevant knowledge---that our work tests at the representational level.

\paragraph{Behavioral analysis of VLAs.}
A growing body of work reveals that VLAs rely disproportionately on visual input.
\cite{grant2026} showed across six architectures that visual pathways dominate action generation, with language instructions ``encoded but not used'' when visual context uniquely specifies the task.
Hou and Zhao~(2026) and Fei et al.~(2025) corroborated this through semantic perturbations and controlled robustness tests on LIBERO, finding that models largely ignore language instructions.
These studies establish the behavioral phenomenon; we provide a representational account showing that action-relevant geometric structure originates in the frozen vision encoder and is invariant to both LLM training and instruction content.

\paragraph{Mechanistic interpretability of VLAs.}
Recent work has probed VLA internals from several angles.
\cite{haon2025} identified sparse semantic directions in OpenVLA causally linked to action selection, enabling activation steering without fine-tuning.
Swann et al.~(2026) applied sparse autoencoders, finding features dominated by memorized sequences with some interpretable motion primitives; Rizzardo et al.~(2026) introduced feature-observability and controllability concepts for VLA steering.
Lu et al.~(2025) and Molinari et al.~(2025) probed OpenVLA layers, extracting symbolic states and world-model representations respectively.
These studies analyze individual features or single components; we complement them with a systematic decomposition quantifying each architectural component's contribution to action structure, with trained-versus-untrained controls absent from all prior work.

\paragraph{Vision encoder representations.}
Our analysis leverages three encoders spanning different pretraining objectives: SigLIP~\cite{zhai2023_siglip} (OpenVLA's frozen VL encoder), CLIP~\cite{radford2021_clip} (independent VL baseline), and DINOv2~\cite{oquab2024_dinov2} (vision-only control), all at ViT-L/14 scale.
Comparing VL-pretrained and vision-only encoders at matched architecture isolates the contribution of language grounding to action-relevant structure.
Relatedly, Fang et al.~(2025) showed that VLA fine-tuning erodes original VLM reasoning abilities, consistent with our finding that fine-tuning does not improve the geometric structure inherited from the vision encoder.

\paragraph{Representational similarity analysis.}
We adopt RSA~\cite{kriegeskorte2008} and CKA~\cite{kornblith2019} as complementary geometric metrics, paired with linear probes~\cite{alain2017} for functional evaluation.
This multi-metric approach proves essential: we show that geometric alignment and functional decodability can dissociate (e.g., DINOv2 matches VL encoders on probe $R^2$ but not RSA), revealing distinct aspects of representation quality relevant to VLA design.

\paragraph{Positioning.}
Our work is distinguished from prior VLA analyses by three features.
First, we perform a \emph{component-level} representational decomposition---separately quantifying vision encoder, projector, and each LLM layer---rather than analyzing individual features or the model as a whole.
Second, we introduce trained-versus-untrained controls that isolate the effect of VLA fine-tuning, revealing that geometric structure is training-invariant while functional routing requires it.
Third, we combine geometric and functional metrics with instruction ablation, providing converging evidence that the vision encoder is the \emph{source} and the LLM is the \emph{router} of action-relevant structure---complementing the behavioral evidence of \cite{grant2026}, the mechanistic directions of \cite{haon2025}, and the feature-level analyses of Swann et al.~(2026).
